text:
alex_h: FYI got a support ticket from AcmeCorp — they're seeing auth failures and huge latency when hitting our /v1/generate endpoint, and they're seeing an audit alert for cross-region residency.

maria.c: Ticket says requests coming from eu-west but trace shows us-east. Customer insists they're routed to eu.

support_pablo: Customer provided request id 9f3b2a7c and a screenshot of the error: "403: region residency policy exception" + `x-request-id: 9f3b2a7c`. They also pasted a curl repro.

jess: Can you drop the minimal repro here? Also are they on Redwood Dedicated or hosted?

support_pablo: Hosted API. Repro (from customer):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-rl-large","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1
```
Response: 403 + long latency (~2.2s) before response.

ankur: I pulled logs for request id 9f3b2a7c — initial routing picked eu-west, then failover hit us-east due to pod OOM on eu-west pool. Fallback happened after 1.9s. The auth check runs at final serving node which is in us-east -> triggers residency violation for this EU-only customer.

alex_h: That matches the customer's audit alert: they got a compliance notification that their data was processed in us-east. We need to treat this as a policy exception and notify security/legal.

compliance_bot: ALERT: Data residency exception detected for tenant=acmecorp, original_region=eu-west-1, final_region=us-east-1, policy=eu_only, severity=high. AuditID=AUD-20260317-4401

jess: Next steps: (1) give customer clear explanation + remediation, (2) reproduce internally and document root cause, (3) prevent further cross-region fallback for eu-only tenants.

ankur: Repro steps I used: throttle eu-west pool to simulate OOM then send 50 concurrent requests with region=eu-west-1 and tenant header `X-Tenant: acmecorp`. Observed failover after 1.9s, auth check at target region, audit event emitted. Logs:
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:44Z] route: lookup -> eu-west-1
[2026-03-17T10:12:46Z] serve: eu-west pod 12 OOM -> mark unhealthy
[2026-03-17T10:12:46Z] router: fallback -> us-east-1 (policy: allow_fallback=false overridden by runtime)
[2026-03-17T10:12:47Z] auth: tenant-check failed -> residency_violation
```

support_pablo: Customer asked for immediate mitigation — asked to pin traffic to eu-west or pause cross-region fallback. What can we do asap?

ankur: Short-term: we can add a tenant tag to the routing policy to block cross-region fallback for tenants with `residency=eu-only`. I can push a config flip that rejects fallback within 10m. Would need SRE to approve.

sre_oncall: I can stage a fast rollback: create a routing rule `deny_fallback_for_tenant: acmecorp` and roll that out to the router fleet in canary then prod. Will need a CIDR-safe deploy window.

alex_h: Also need a customer-facing message and an internal incident note. Jess — can you draft the message to AcmeCorp? Include apology, confirm we will disable cross-region fallback for them, provide timeline and ask if they want data residency impact report.

jess: Drafting now. Proposed text: "We're investigating an unintended cross-region failover that caused requests to be processed outside EU. We've disabled cross-region fallback for your tenant, are compiling an audit report, and will follow up with remediation steps. Full email in 20m." Thoughts?

compliance_bot: NOTE: Please file a policy exception ticket (PEX-385) and attach auditID AUD-20260317-4401.

billing-bot: Heads-up: customer also reported a spike in token charges during the incident window. Recommend we open a billing dispute review.

support_pablo: Confirming customer wants a SOC-style audit log and a credit for any tokens processed outside region.

alex_h: OK — assign tasks: ankur -> routing config change (short-term block), sre_oncall -> rollout, jess -> customer comms + audit report, compliance_bot -> open PEX and notify legal, billing-bot -> start billing review. Keep updates here.

jess: sent initial message to customer and legal looped in. Will attach repro logs and a timeline once ankur confirms routing change.

ankur: Routing change staged to canary at 10:40Z, looks good. No fallback for canary requests. Rolling to prod now.

sre_oncall: Prod rollout complete at 10:52Z. Can confirm no cross-region fallback for tenant `acmecorp` in the subsequent 30 minutes of traffic.

alex_h: Great. Closing immediate escalation. Next: longer term fix to ensure auth checks occur before final failover decision (or route fail early), and add per-tenant residency flag in provisioning. Filing followups in product/tech backlog.

support_pablo: Customer acknowledged and asked for timeline for permanent fix — gave ETA 2 weeks.

jess: Incident summary saved to /incidents/1872109876 and PEX ticket opened.

compliance_bot: RESOLVED: AUD-20260317-4401 linked to PEX-385.
